t: That in any case in which the renewal term of copyright subsisting in any work on the date of approval of this resolution, or the term thereof as extended by Public Law 87–668, by Public Law 89–142, by Public Law 90–141, by Public Law 90–416, by Public Law 91–147, or by Public Law 91–555 (or by all or certain of said laws), would expire prior to December 31, 1972, such term is hereby continued until December 31, 1972.

fable.w: This provision extends the renewal term of existing copyrights by direct operation of law until a fixed date. There is no tempting participation reading: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no outside party plays any role in a federal decision.
fable.s: such term is hereby continued until December 31, 1972.

opus.w: This section only extends renewal copyright terms that would otherwise expire to December 31, 1972. It does not require or allow any consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue. Copyright holders benefit, but they play no part in any federal decision, so this is not participation.
opus.b: The tempting reading would be that a copyright extension touches outside parties, since copyright holders benefit. But nobody outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to object or sue. Congress simply extends the terms by statute.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply extends the duration of copyright terms for specific works. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or experts) before making this decision. The action is a direct legislative mandate without any procedural requirement for outside input.
qwen_chat.s: That in any case in which the renewal term of copyright subsisting in any work on the date of approval of this resolution... such term is hereby continued until December 31, 1972.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that extending copyright terms affects the public or creators, but the text itself contains no mechanism for public input, consultation, or participation. It is a unilateral legislative act extending a legal term.
